notes.text: Issuer identity is legal-entity based and never resolved from a ticker string. Several issuers are placed on more than one link because they are genuinely vertically integrated (MP Materials on separation, metal-alloy, and mining/feedstock; Energy Fuels on separation, metal-alloy via its pending Vacuumschmelze deal, magnet manufacturing via the same deal, and feedstock via White Mesa) — this mirrors the chain's own capture_inputs notes flagging the same overlap as intentional, not double counting.

Five listing identity_evidence items (MP, Energy Fuels, American Resources, REalloys, USA Rare Earth, Compass Diversified: six in total) were extracted via WebFetch's prompted reading of an SEC EDGAR iXBRL cover page rather than a locally verified pdftotext pass on a saved PDF. Four other identity items (Neo Performance Materials, Solvay, Lockheed Martin, Energy Fuels' own 10-Q was in fact PDF-verified) were confirmed by saving the source PDF and running pdftotext directly, giving a stronger provenance guarantee. This distinction matters for a future semantic audit: the WebFetch-mediated extractions reconstruct the standard SEC cover-page template (verified twice this session against true pdftotext ground truth on Lockheed Martin and Energy Fuels) rather than being independently character-verified for each specific filing.

China's incumbent mining-to-magnet complex (china-incumbent-complex, position 1, CHOKE_POINT) is the largest gap in this census: Shanghai and Shenzhen Stock Exchange official pages were not fetchable this session (404s and connection resets on every attempted URL pattern), so despite four plausible candidate tickers already named on the chain, zero placements could be recorded against the official-evidence bar. This is a genuine access limitation, not a finding that fewer than five Chinese-listed issuers exist.
